meta.source_system: PPP Link Control Protocol option-negotiation automaton (one automaton as seen by one endpoint), transcribed from RFC 1661 section 4 and its sec.4.1 State Transition Table. RFC 1661 is a public standard (Internet Standards Track; STD 51).
meta.source_citation: RFC 1661 (July 1994), section 4 'The Option Negotiation Automaton', sec.4.1 State Transition Table (both halves, all 16 event rows x 10 state columns) + footnotes p/r/x + sec.4.2 States + sec.4.3 Events. Per-edge citations with snapshot line numbers in meta.edges_with_citations.
meta.semantics_class: event: the actions are protocol events (the table's own row labels Up/Down/Open/Close/TO+/-/RCR+/-/RCA/RCN/RTR/RTA/RUC/RXJ+/-/RXR); their names are part of the behavior and do not follow state renamings -- candidate groups in groups/ declare semantics "fixed". The relabel rows in expected.json are the diagnostic contrast reading, not the protocol-true one.
meta.encoding: states 10..15 = unreachable padding (self-loop only); undeclared (state, event) pairs and the table's '-' illegal-transition cells self-loop with reward 0
meta.reward_rule: rewards all zero: the negotiation automaton defines no payoff; the reward layer carries no information, all conclusions come from the transition layer

transcription_notes: KEPT (one event, three packets): RXR bundles Receive-Echo-Request / Receive-Echo-Reply / Receive-Discard-Request into a single event: the sec.4 preamble says these packet classes 'are not differentiated in the automaton descriptions ... they always cause the same transitions' (snapshot txt:676-681); the table has one RXR row (txt:758 / txt:803); sec.4.3 defines it (txt:1201-1207).

KEPT (actions not modeled): each table cell is action/new-state (sec.4.1 preamble txt:726-729). The transcription keeps the transition target; the action lists (tlu/tld/tls/tlf, irc/zrc, scr/sca/scn, str/sta, scj, ser) are not part of the model layer -- the model encodes (state, event) -> state only, the same transition-layer-only policy as the tcp and http2 cases. The printed cell text stays visible in every edge citation.

NOT COLLECTED ('-' cells): the dash marks an illegal transition (sec.4.1 preamble txt:730-732); 40 of the 160 cells are '-' (Up x states 2..5 txt:738 and x states 6..9 txt:783, Down x Initial/Starting txt:739, TO+ and TO- x states 0..3 txt:743-744 and x Opened txt:788-789, the four receive rows x Initial/Starting txt:746-749 and RTR/RTA/RUC/RXJ+/RXJ-/RXR x Initial/Starting, Up already counted). They encode 'this event does not occur here' and collapse to the same self-loop as undeclared pairs (reward 0), per the tcp/http2 encoding policy.

KEPT (declared self-transitions): 67 of the 120 declared cells carry a new state equal to the source state (e.g. Open in Starting is plain '1' txt:740, Close in Initial is '0' txt:741, TO+ in Closing is 'str/4' txt:743, RTA in Req-Sent is '6' txt:797, RUC in Opened is 'scj/9' txt:799). All are transcribed as ordinary edges (from == to) so the collected edge set mirrors the table cell for cell; in the trans matrix they coincide numerically with self-loops.

NOT COLLECTED (footnote semantics): the table's footnote letters p/r/x (txt:818/820/822) annotate implementation options -- Passive, Restart, crossed connection -- that change actions or reading, not the new-state column. The letters are quoted in the affected edges' citations and the option discussions are anchored (p: txt:894-904, r: txt:1025-1041, x: txt:1124-1135).

NOT COLLECTED (cross-layer propagation): This-Layer-Up/Down actions signal NCP automata (sec.4.3 'Up' txt:979-986, 'Down' txt:1004-1006); that inter-automaton signaling is outside this case's scope (one LCP automaton, one endpoint).

KEPT (state naming): state_names use the printed table-header abbreviations Req-Sent / Ack-Rcvd / Ack-Sent (txt:736, txt:781); sec.4.2 prints the long forms Request-Sent (txt:931) and Ack-Received (txt:945).
